source.quote: iFi audio's own page for the NEO iDSD 3, read 2026-11-24 in a browser (the host returns 429 to automated fetchers), from the page's « Specifications » block: « DIGITAL INPUTS Bluetooth 5.4; USB-B 3.0; S/PDIF Coaxial; S/PDIF Optical; »; « FILE SUPPORT 768kHz PCM; DSD512 (22.6 MHz) »; « ANALOGUE INPUTS Single-Ended RCA (L/R) »; « BLUETOOTH FORMATS aptX Lossless, aptX Adaptive, aptX, LDAC, LHDC/HWA, AAC, SBC »; « SNR+DNR >=120dB(A) @ -60dBFS »; « THD+N <=0.0015% @ 0dBFS »; « LINE OUTPUTS Balanced XLR (L/R): <=19.5V (variable); 4.4V (fixed) ». The block ends with the page's own « Note: Specifications are subject to change without notice ». No DAC chip, no digital filter and no bit depth appear anywhere in it. Self-description: « Merging purist design principles with the latest features from across our range, the NEO iDSD brings the best of iFi audio together in a complete, all-in-one home audio package. »

facts.chip: Not named on this page. iFi's brand-level evidence - « All iFi DACs that support DSD and are using TI/BB chipset » - does not reach a particular model, so no family is asserted here either.

_un_seul_chiffre_pour_toutes_les_entrees: iFi publishes ONE « HI-RES SUPPORT » or « FILE SUPPORT » line for the whole device and never breaks it down by input. No inputs block is written here, and that is a decision the catalogue has already paid for: on 2026-11-20 the ifi/generique record carried per-input ceilings spread from exactly this kind of global line, and they were WITHDRAWN on the maker's own manual, which says « Inputs other than USB are currently limited to maximum sample rates of 192kHz PCM and DSD64 via DoP ». A global figure on an iFi page is therefore known to be the USB figure, and spreading it across coaxial and optical would overstate them by a factor of four.
_aptx_lossless_et_ldac_sur_une_entree_sa: « BLUETOOTH FORMATS aptX Lossless, aptX Adaptive, aptX, LDAC, LHDC/HWA, AAC, SBC » - seven codecs named, and not one rate or bit depth for the Bluetooth input. The Chord Hugo 2 and the Cambridge DacMagic 200M both rate theirs (48 kHz/16 bit and 16 bit), so the figure is publishable; this maker lists the codecs instead. No bluetooth block is written: a codec name is not a ceiling, and aptX Lossless and SBC are nothing like each other.
